_comment_not_in_battery: Several rules are verified outside this ART battery, all documented in phase-4-detection/sigma/README.md and proven by phase-4-detection/sigma/sigma-selftest.py: (1) T1105 AND T1027 certutil download (rules 100500/1 — both rules tag BOTH technique IDs in the same <mitre> block, confirmed 2026-09-23 by reading the rule XML directly, not inferred) — Microsoft Defender kills certutil download before it spawns, so there's no telemetry for either technique (defense-in-depth, not a gap). (2) T1562.001 Defender exclusion via PowerShell (ps_script rule 100506) — this host's offline Atomic Red Team bundle has no T1562.001 atomic, so it was live-fired manually (Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath) to prove the ps_script->Wazuh path fires end-to-end, then the exclusion was removed. (3) T1560.001 (archive staging, rules 100517-519) — no offline-viable ART atomic exists (the rar/7-Zip/WinZip tests all require downloading the installer; the one self-contained test uses .NET ZipFile, not the Compress-Archive cmdlet the ps_script rule keys on) — validated instead via a direct Compress-Archive invocation in ad-validate.py. (4) T1047/T1021.006/T1569.002 (WMI/WinRM/PsExec lateral movement, rules 100513-516) and T1190 (DMZ web attack, rules 100440-442) aren't ws-01-local ART atomics at all — they're attacks launched FROM atk-01 (against ws-01 or dmz-01), so they live in ad-validate.py alongside the AD attack scenarios, which already models exactly that shape. (5) T1490 rule 100522 (wmic shadowcopy delete) — ART test 2 ('Windows - Delete Volume Shadow Copies via WMI') is correctly mapped, but wmic.exe does not exist on this ws-01 build (Windows 11 25H2 dropped it; verified 2026-09-06: Test-Path on both System32\\wmic.exe and System32\\wbem\\WMIC.exe returns False, Get-Command finds nothing) — an environment/tooling gap, not a rule defect; the rule's logic is unchanged and still correct for any host that has wmic. NOTE ON TEST NUMBERING: the ART test numbers actually on disk (`Invoke-AtomicTest T1490 -ShowDetailsBrief`) do not match the technique's public GitHub numbering 1:1 on this offline-installed copy — test 9 here is 'Disable System Restore Through Registry', not vssadmin resize (that's test 10). Confirmed by listing tests directly on ws-01, not by trusting a remembered/fetched number; the original T1490 entry above was off by one for exactly this reason before being fixed. CORRECTION (2026-09-07): T1003.001 comsvcs (100525) was excluded here overnight as 'Defender-blocked, no Sysmon telemetry' — that was wrong. Fresh testing showed Sysmon DOES capture the rundll32/comsvcs process-creation event (Defender's action happens after, denying the actual memory read/dump write, not the process launch), and rule 100525 fires reliably (9 real hits across the session, including one from a test run specifically to double-check this correction). Re-added to the active battery. 100526 (the companion rundll32+lsass rule) never independently registers — it's a same-level sibling of 100525 matching the identical event, and Wazuh's one-alert-per-event model only ever records one of two co-matching same-level rules; not itself evidence either rule is broken. (6) T1218.005/T1218.011 (mshta/rundll32 script-moniker LOLBins, rules 100116/100115) — ART's own atomics for these (mshta-vbscript, rundll32-vbscript) don't just error, one (T1218.011-2) crashed the WinRM/SSH session outright on 2026-09-12, matching the pre-existing 'ART harness .Start() Access is denied' finding but worse; validated instead via a direct, timeout-guarded Start-Process invocation (`mshta.exe vbscript:close` / `rundll32.exe vbscript:close`) in ad-validate.py, same reasoning as T1560.001 above. T1218.010 (regsvr32, 100114) and T1548.002 (both rules, 100117/100118) DID work cleanly through the standard ART harness and are in the active battery above. UPDATE (2026-09-13): the 2026-09-07 correction above no longer reproduces — a fresh live-fire (both via Invoke-AtomicTest and a direct rundll32/comsvcs.dll invocation, bypassing the harness entirely) got 'Access is denied' at process launch, not just at the memory-read step, and zero Sysmon telemetry either way. Left in the active battery rather than pulled, since the underlying rule logic is unchanged and correct — but this is now believed to be genuinely flaky over time (Defender's real-time heuristics evidently tightened between the two checks, an environment drift outside this repo's control, not a rule regression) rather than a settled 'proven reliable' result. Re-verify before trusting a FAIL here as a rule defect.
